newsitem.title: UK: Britain's housing market accelerates into new year.
newsitem.headline: Britain's housing market accelerates into new year.

text.p: Britain's housing market is enjoying its longest uninterrupted run of growth for almost 20 years and the outlook for 1997 is even stronger, the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) said.
December was "uncharacteristically strong" with evidence of buyers confirming deals the day before Christmas, according to some estate agents.

"It seems that the forthcoming general election, the neutral budget and the threat of further interest rate rises did nothing to dampen the market," RICS said in its housing market survey, which covers the three months to December.
The average number of properties for sale plunged by 40 percent, its lowest point for eight years, fuelling competition among buyers.
Overall December saw the sixteenth consecutive month- on-month increase in the percentage of contributors reporting price rises, the longest period of uninterrupted growth since 1978.
"As inflationary pressure mounts, it is unlikely that the Bank of England or the government will allow this level of growth to continue unchecked," said RICS housing spokesman Ian Perry.
"Further interest rates and the abolition of MIRAS (mortgage interest relief at source) look increasingly likely."
But he said prices were set to remain on an upward trend throughout this year and warned first-time buyers should not delay unnecessarily.
